question: Based on evidence from seismic waves, heat flows and meteorites, which layer of Earth is made up of rock that represents 84% of the Earth's total volume?
solution:
The correct answer is Mantle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **mantle** takes up an **astounding 84%** of the entire volume of the** Earth** and is roughly **2,900 kilometres (1,802 miles) thick**. Partially **melted rock** makes up some of the **mantle's molten regions**.
 
• The **core** is encircled by a thick mantle of rock, primarily silicates.
 
• The **molten rock** in the mantle is continually moving. It is propelled to the surface at **mid-ocean ridges and during volcanic eruptions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Inner core**

 
 
• The** innermost geologic stratum** of the planet Earth is called the** inner core**. It is mostly a solid ball with a radius of **1,220 km**, which is around **20%** of the radius of the Earth or **70% of the radius of the Moon.**
 
 
 
• **Outer core**
 
 
• Above the **Earth's solid inner core** and beneath its mantle is a fluid layer inner core of the Earth; beneath its mantle is a **fluid layer roughly 2,260 km thick** and primarily made of iron and nickel.
 
 
 
• **Oceanic crust**
 
 
• **Basalt and gabbro are two types of dark-coloured rocks** that make up the majority of the oceanic crust. Compared to continental crust, which is composed of **andesite and granite,** which are light-coloured rocks, it is both thinner and denser.
